correctness.rationale: The proof accounts for unnormalized 2π arc length and full periodic variation. General positive even-kernel leakage is exactly an arc flux, and periodic BV coarea plus strict positivity give all-function norm and equality. The finite Fejér Fourier expansion yields the odd-frequency constant; near π the sine quotient has nonzero value at odd degrees and quadratic zero at even degrees, giving quadratic vs quartic arc deficit. Euler–Maclaurin gives the parity cubic law with O(n^-5). The actual standalone checker passed 96 Fourier/quadrature, 36 local parity, 6 asymptotic, and 240 sampled BV tests; numerical tests are corroboration only. Limits: ordinary Fejér kernel, all integer n>=1, real periodic BV.

value.rationale: A canonical positive Fourier approximator receives a sharp exact all-degree integrated L1 error budget over discontinuous real BV data and a complete extremizer classification. The different quadratic (odd degree) versus quartic (even degree) stability deficit of nearly semicircular jump pairs is structural and useful for sensitivity to jump location. The signed cubic parity correction resolves a nontrivial refinement of its logarithmic convergence rate. These are precise natural invariants, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
